sources.title: Percent Above Moving Average
sources.publisher_type: technical chart education, not an exchange or regulator
sources.readback: Reused current-chat primary page opened in preceding turn; text supplied in tool output
sources.indicator: percentage of stocks above their own simple moving averages

facts.meaning: Conventional oversold/overbought examples; levels may vary with the index. Strong trends can keep readings extreme; low level alone is not a buy signal.
A majority-participation reference, discussed for150/200-day breadth; crossings can whipsaw. No symmetric top/bottom bands inferred.

sources.scope: US-index examples including S&P500 for50-day and S&P100 for200-day; all-A transfer not validated
sources.adoption: compact fixed-reference row, distinct from local P10/P90; no20/100-day values invented

sources.indicator: S&P500 percentage above own50-day moving average

facts.meaning: Around80% while the index rallies is broad bullish participation, not automatic overbought or top.
Below10% in a selloff can indicate overdone selling; explicitly does not establish the selloff is over.
Longer-horizon investor context; no fixed200-day extreme thresholds supplied in this article.

sources.scope: S&P500; article illustration includes April-May2025, not a backtest
sources.adoption: US compact source comparison and source details; never transpose80 to a sell risk line; noCN endorsement
